statement_record.book: For a rig R, the prop Mat(R) is ISOMORPHIC to the prop presented by the generator set G_R - add (2->1), zero (0->1), copy (1->2), discard (1->0) and one amplifier a (1->1) for each a in R, the same generators as SFG_R - modulo the drawn equations: (i) copy/discard make the object 1 a cocommutative comonoid; (ii) add/zero make it a commutative monoid; (iii) the two interact as a bimonoid (copy of a sum = two copies added with a middle interchange, discard of a sum = both discarded, copy of zero = two zeros, zero;discard = empty diagram); (iv) the scalars compose (a;b = ab), add (copy;(a (+) b);add = a+b), satisfy 1 = identity wire and 0 = discard;zero, and each commutes with copy, add, discard and zero. Proof by rewriting to the normal form of Proposition 5.56 (black nodes left, scalars middle, white nodes right). Stated consequence: the graphical rules are a SOUND and COMPLETE reasoning system - two signal flow graphs denote the same matrix iff one rewrites into the other by these equations plus the prop axioms.

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker, and the headline claim is absent outright: the ISOMORPHISM is not stated anywhere, because neither side exists - no rig R (item def5.36 is PARTIAL, only Structure/Preadditive.v's enrichment laws), no Mat(R) at all, no G_R signature, no E_R equation system - and no concrete prop in the tree is ever proved isomorphic to a presented one, so neither the normal-form/completeness argument nor even the soundness direction is instantiated. What exists is (a) the general presented-prop apparatus, already credited at def5.33 / remark5.34 (Construction/PROP/Presentation.v:312 PresentedPROP; Construction/PROP/Presentation/Universal.v:139 ESound, :180 interpW_sound, :340 Presented_factor, :435 Presented_unique) - this is precisely the machine that would build the comparison functor Presented(G_R,E_R) ⟶ Mat(R) and discharge the SOUNDNESS half of the sound-and-complete claim, in a form general over any signature, any equation system and any target PROP; and (b) three fragments of the equation list. Of those fragments, SupplyEqs is the closest in kind (a real generators-and-equations presentation of copy/discard as a cocommutative comonoid) but is COLOURED, per-copyable-colour, and carries clause (i) only. biproduct_addition is on the semantic side, not the syntactic one: it is an equation between morphisms of a preadditive category with biproducts (the enrichment is assumed, not presented), and the one-object delooping that would turn it into the book's scalar axiom is never taken in-tree (see def5.36). CommutativeMonoid/CommutativeComonoid/CopyDiscard state clauses (i) and (ii) as abstract object structure rather than as prop equations.
